record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Carry out the full constructive program for the superconducting BCS phase of interacting fermions in two dimensions, including the intermediate 1/N regime, gluing to earlier scales, and the long-distance Goldstone-boson regime.

evidence.quote: In two dimensions there is a well-defined strategy which should lead ultimately to the complete construction of the BCS2 model, namely the control of the BCS phase at zero temperature

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of non-relativistic spin-1/2 interacting fermions in two spatial dimensions with a rotation-invariant Fermi surface and a weak local attractive two-body interaction (a 2D analog of the BCS Hamiltonian). Working in the Euclidean functional-integral formulation at temperature T = 0, develop a fully rigorous (constructive) renormalization-group construction of the model, encompassing all of the following:

1. Control of the high- and intermediate-energy regime down to the BCS energy scale, with convergent multiscale expansions and uniform bounds on the Schwinger functions.

2. Treatment of the intermediate 1/N regime (where N is the effective number of sectors covering an annulus around the Fermi surface), including a rigorous bosonization/auxiliary-field expansion that exhibits the formation of Cooper pairs and produces a non-vanishing pairing condensate (anomalous two-point function) at temperatures below a critical scale T_c > 0.

3. Gluing the 1/N expansion to the previously controlled higher-energy scales so that the effective action obtained at the BCS scale is the rigorous output of the integration over higher modes.

4. Construction of the long-distance regime dominated by the gapless Goldstone boson associated to the spontaneously broken U(1) phase symmetry, including a proof of long-range order (or quasi-long-range order, as appropriate in two dimensions) and the determination of the asymptotic decay of the pair–pair correlation function.

Prove, in particular, the existence of an infinite-volume limit of the model with a non-trivial superconducting (BCS) phase, and characterize the decay of the relevant correlation functions in this phase.
artifact.status_search_result: No published rigorous construction of the full BCS phase for two-dimensional interacting fermions, including the gluing of scales and the Goldstone long-distance regime, was found in the literature search. Partial constructive results exist for the high-energy and 1/N regimes of related 2D Fermi systems, but the full program as stated does not appear to have been carried out, so the problem is regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Goldstone and Higgs Hydrodynamics in the BCS–BEC Crossover
status_evidence.snippet: Effective field theory of Goldstone/Higgs modes in BCS–BEC crossover, treated at the level of physics rather than rigorous constructive QFT.
status_evidence.claim: Existing analyses of 2D BCS Goldstone modes are physics-level, not a rigorous constructive construction.

status_evidence.title: BCS theory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Standard BCS theory is a mean-field approach; rigorous mathematical construction in 2D with Goldstone regime is not part of the established theory.
status_evidence.claim: No standard reference establishes a fully rigorous 2D BCS construction including the Goldstone regime.
